items.q: On a screen of 1920 by 1080 pixels, which position is the lower-right corner for pyautogui?
rationales: Positions start at 0, so the last column is 1919 and the last row 1079.
The x value comes first.

items.q: pyautogui.moveTo(5000, 5000) is called on a 1920 by 1080 screen. Where does the pointer end, and what does moveTo(-50, -50) give?
options: (1919, 1079) and (0, 0): the pointer stops at the screen edge
It raises an error for both
rationales: On the recorded virtual display no error was raised for these values.
The pointer cannot leave the screen.

items.q: The fail-safe was triggered by moving the pointer to (0, 0). In the recorded run, which calls raised FailSafeException afterwards?
options: click(), write() and moveTo(), while position(), size() and screenshot() still ran
rationales: Other calls that act on the screen raise it too.
The functions that only read the screen kept working.

items.q: What is the default value of pyautogui.PAUSE?
rationales: Mouse and keyboard calls wait after each call.
One second would make a drawing program very slow.

items.q: In the recorded run moveTo(900, 700, duration=0.1) made one motion event and moveTo(900, 700, duration=1.0) made 21. What does that show?
options: The pointer jumps when the duration is no longer than the pause between steps, and moves in small steps for a long one
The pointer moved once per second
rationales: The duration worked on the Linux virtual display.
21 motion events in one second are about 20 a second, not one.

items.q: In the recorded run click(clicks=2, interval=0.6) and doubleClick() both sent two presses. How did they differ?
options: doubleClick() produced a DoubleClick event; the slow clicks, 0.6 seconds apart, did not
rationales: The program that listened to the events saw a difference.
Two presses were sent in both.

items.q: pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'c') is called. In which order did the recorded events arrive?
options: Press ctrl, press c, release c, release ctrl
Press ctrl, release ctrl, press c, release c
Press c, press ctrl, release c, release ctrl
rationales: The keys are held together, so ctrl is released last.
The first key named is pressed first.

items.q: In the recorded run press('nokey') and write(['a', 'b']) raised no error, while write(42) raised TypeError. What should a script not rely on?
options: An unknown key name stopping the program
rationales: write(42) raised TypeError, so it does check its argument.
press('nokey') typed nothing and did not raise.

items.q: On a display with 16 bits of colour the recorded pixel of a grey background was (172, 174, 172) instead of (176, 176, 175) on 24 bits. What happened to pixelMatchesColor() with the 24-bit value?
options: It returned False on the 16-bit display, so a tolerance is needed
rationales: The colours differ, so the exact match failed.
No exception was raised in the recording.

items.q: With PyAutoGUI 0.9.54 and PyScreeze 1.0.1, locateOnScreen() of an image that is not on the screen raised ImageNotFoundException in the recording. What did the old PyScreeze 0.1.28 do?
rationales: The older release returned None instead.
It did not return a box.

items.q: scroll(-1) moved a Tk text window by one line under Tk 9.0.3 and by two lines under Tk 8.6.14 in the recording. What does that show?
options: One scroll unit is not the same number of lines in every environment
rationales: It moved two lines under Tk 8.6.
It moved the text under both.

items.q: A script loops forever sending moveTo(0, 0). Which setting stops it from running away?
options: pyautogui.FAILSAFE = True, which is the default: moving to a screen corner makes the next call raise FailSafeException
rationales: A pause of 0 would only make it faster.
The fail-safe corners exist to stop a runaway script.
